summary: Transient throughput collapse after autoscaler rebalance; GPU memory thrashing and PCIe retransmit symptoms
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled autoscaler rebalance in a dedicated pool for Aurelia Health, several latency-sensitive routes experienced rapid p50->p99 throughput degradation for ~10-20 minutes. Customer reported increased 5xxs and timeouts from application side.

Impact:
- Multiple production tenants (primary: Aurelia Health) saw inference throughput drop by 40-70% and p99 latency spike by 4-8x for affected routes.
- Client-visible timeouts and failed requests to the Redwood API for ~15 minutes.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-3 (reserved GPUs: A100-40GB)
- Cluster autoscaler initiated a rebalance due to new node scale-in event at ~2026-03-10T03:17:00Z.
- Affected model: redwood/llama2-7b-q4f16 pinned by customer.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Autoscaler triggers scale-in and the scheduler rebalances pods across nodes (rebalance window starts).
2) After placement changes, several GPU allocations show elevated memory churn and repeated small reallocations (observed in nvml counters).
3) Within 1-2 minutes of placement, serving runtime begins to queue more requests; per-GPU PCIe retransmit counters and kernel logs show increased I/O retries.
4) Throughput and p99 latency degrade until autoscaler finishes and affected pods are either evicted or rebalanced again.

Observed behavior:
- p50 remained relatively stable, but p95/p99 and total throughput dropped sharply.
- nvidia-smi showed frequent transient memory spikes and context switches on impacted GPUs.
- dmesg showed non-fatal PCIe link retries on the underlying hosts during the incident window.
- Serving runtime logs report repeated KV cache miss/flush cycles coincident with memory churn.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler rebalance should not cause sustained throughput collapse for pinned dedicated workloads.

Logs/links:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/throughput/dedicated-pool-overview?var-pool=dp-us-east-3
- Support trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/SUP-812407
- Kernel logs (excerpt): host-node-57 dmesg 2026-03-10 03:18:12 -> "PCIE AER: Corrected error, ID 0x0002"
comments: 2026-03-10 03:25 Support (Leah Martinez): Customer reported timeouts and supplied SDK logs showing 504s. Opened incident and began initial triage.
2026-03-10 03:40 SRE (Rajesh Patel): Noted autoscaler rebalance window at 03:17Z; correlating pod move events with throughput drops. Investigating node-level PCIe counters.
2026-03-10 04:05 Customer (Aurelia Health - ops@aurelia): Confirmed failures aligned with our peak inference window; requested immediate workaround to stop rebalance or isolate their pods.
2026-03-10 04:20 Support (Leah Martinez): Applied temporary affinity annotation to keep Aurelia pods on pre-existing nodes; observed throughput recovery within 6 minutes.
2026-03-11 09:12 Infra (Marta Gomez): Collected nvml counters and host PCIe stats. Found transient incremental increases in PCIe retransmit/serr_corrected counters on 3 hosts in dp-us-east-3.

2026-03-12 11:30 Eng (Rajesh Patel): Reproduced memory-churn pattern in controlled canary when performing rapid pod shuffle with similar model workload; observed small-range GPU memory thrashing in the runtime causing KV cache flush behavior.
2026-03-12 17:05 Eng (Rajesh Patel): Opened scheduler PR to add cooldown to rebalance and prefer anti-affinity for high-memory pinned pods (see linked PR).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Rapid pod relocation caused KV cache misses + eager memory reallocation in the runtime, driving PCIe traffic due to host-level page migration and NVLINK/PCIE transfers.
Hypothesis 2: Underlying host NIC or PCIe fabric experienced transient corrected errors which, combined with high memory churn, amplified request serialization on GPUs.
Evidence gathered: nvml per-process memory graphs show repeated small allocations/releases around the time of eviction; host-level pcie_aer counters incremented on node-57, node-63, node-61.
Commands run: collected nvidia-smi dmon, nvml query snapshots, 'dmesg | grep -i aer', and kernel PCIe counters from /sys/class/pci_bus/0000:00/*/aer/*.

Controlled repro: Ran a canary that simulates the customer's mix of small streaming and medium batch requests; when forcing a scheduler reshuffle we observed the same transient throughput collapse and elevated pcie retries.
Correlation: Throughput collapse aligns tightly with period of repeated KV cache flushes in serving runtime (logs attached to trace), not with raw GPU thermal throttling or full memory exhaustion.
Temporary mitigation validated: pinning pods to nodes avoided the issue; increasing autoscaler rebalance cooldown to 10m reduced frequency.
resolution_notes: Immediate workaround (applied 2026-03-10 04:20Z): Added node-affinity to Aurelia Health's deployment to prevent rebalance during peak hours; customer throughput restored.

Short-term fix (rolled 2026-03-12): Scheduler change to introduce a 600s cooldown window before rebalancing pods in a pool when any pod is using a pinned GPU model; prefer node anti-affinity for workloads flagged high-memory/kv-cache.

Medium-term actions (in progress): Update scheduler heuristics to detect high churn KV-cache patterns and avoid colocating the same workload on nodes undergoing heavy PCIe retry events; add an autoscaler safety check that pauses scale-in if PCIe corrected errors are increasing.

Long-term follow-ups: Patch serving runtime to reduce eager KV cache flush on relocation (engineering ticket created), upgrade host PCIe firmware on impacted hardware in dp-us-east-3 during the maintenance window, and add a Grafana alert for PCIE corrected error rate crossing threshold.
Post-incident: Customer notified of root-cause hypotheses and short-term mitigations; follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-16 to coordinate dedicated pool sizing and preferred anti-affinity policies.
Status: Mitigations in place and customer operations restored; task remains open until scheduler heuristics and firmware upgrade complete.
